passage: Family diary, Sunday. Noor writing. Our ceiling fan began to wobble, so my brother-in-law came over to fix it. Preeti, my daughter, held the ladder and passed him the tools. First he switched off the fan and the main switch and stuck tape over it with a note. Preeti asked why he loosened the blades one by one. "So they balance," he said, and showed her the small gap on one. She watched his hands more than his face. When the fan ran quietly, she said, "I could do that." He smiled and said, "Next time, you can hold the screwdriver." I have never seen her stand so straight. Noor

passage: Sunday. Rafiq chacha said the back tyre of my cycle was flat again, and instead of doing it himself he said, "Bring the bucket." First he showed me how to take the tube out. Then I filled the bucket and pushed the tube through the water. Tiny bubbles came out of one spot, and chacha put his finger on it. "See? That's your hole." He told me to rough up the rubber, and why the glue needs to dry a little before the patch. I did the patch with my own hands. It looked ugly but held air. I rode round the lane three times. Nobody had to tell me I was proud. Afreen

subtype: Fixing something with a family member [Actor]
passage: I'm Disha, and the ceiling fan in our living room taught me more than any physics class. I was fourteen when it started wobbling and making a clicking sound. My father, Siddharth, said, "Come, hold the ladder, and watch." First he switched off the fan at the main switch. "Always first," he said. Then he climbed up, and I held the ladder steady. He showed me the loose screws on the blade holder, explained that the wobble came from one blade being heavier. He tightened them, and let me hand him each tool, telling me why he chose it. When the fan turned smoothly again, he said, "Your turn next time." That feeling of being able to fix things never left me.

qa.q: What did Siddharth do first before climbing up?
qa.a: He switched off the fan at the main switch.

qa.q: How did Disha feel when the fan turned smoothly again?
qa.a: Disha felt proud and capable, a feeling that never left.

qa.q: What made this a good way for Disha to learn?
qa.a: Watching his hands, handing him tools and hearing why each step and tool mattered, starting with switching off the power.

qa.q: How might Siddharth feel teaching Disha?
qa.a: He likely felt proud and pleased, passing on his skill and trusting Disha with the next repair.

grounding: A young adult recalls helping a parent fix a fan as a teenager, learning by watching and hearing why, and gaining lasting capability.

passage:
Note from Minakshi (Madhav's aunt), written for his school's "skills at home" project, Sunday.
This morning Madhav, fifteen, helped his uncle fix the leaking kitchen tap. His uncle first showed him how to close the main valve under the sink. Madhav watched closely as the tap was opened and a worn rubber washer taken out. His uncle explained why the washer wears out and let Madhav fit the new one himself. Madhav's hands were unsure at first; he dropped the washer twice. But when the tap was closed and the dripping stopped, he grinned widely and said, "I did that." He has asked to help with the cycle chain next weekend.

qa.q: What part did Madhav fit himself?
qa.a: The new rubber washer.

qa.q: How did Madhav feel when the dripping stopped?
qa.a: He felt proud and capable, grinning widely and saying, "I did that."

qa.q: What made this a good way for Madhav to learn the repair?
qa.a: His uncle showed each step, explained why the washer wears out, and let Madhav do the fitting himself, even with fumbles.

qa.q: How might Madhav's uncle feel when Madhav asks to help with the cycle chain?
qa.a: His uncle would likely feel pleased and proud that Madhav wants to keep learning with him.

subtype: Fixing something with a family member [Actor]
passage:
Dear Diary, Saturday.
Nani's sewing machine was stuck, so Zeenat Nani called me over. "Come, you have young eyes." She showed me where the thread was jammed under the plate, and made me unscrew two tiny screws. She told me why the thread knots: when it's pulled too tight. We cleaned out old fluff with a paintbrush and put a drop of oil where she pointed. She kept telling me stories about stitching my mother's school uniforms on this very machine. When it started humming again, Nani clapped. I felt so capable. Tomorrow she's teaching me how to thread it properly.
Vinita

qa.q: What did Vinita use to clean out the old fluff?
qa.a: A paintbrush.

qa.q: How did Vinita feel when the machine started humming again?
qa.a: Vinita felt capable and proud as Nani clapped.

qa.q: What made Nani a good teacher for this repair?
qa.a: She showed each step, explained why the thread knots and let Vinita do the unscrewing and cleaning herself.

qa.q: How might Zeenat Nani feel sharing this with Vinita?
qa.a: Nani likely felt happy and close to Vinita, passing on a skill and memories of stitching uniforms on the same machine.

grounding: A teenager's diary shows fixing a sewing machine with a grandmother, learning by watching and hearing why.

Rehana: [photo]
Rehana: it clicks now!! smooth like butter
Uma: ok engineer 😄

Rehana: I feel weirdly proud of a lock
